solutions.check: grid and clues read from the FT's printable PDF, its numbering matching the clue list; every fifteensquared answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Captain of industry, eg, to hamper changes

indicators.note: changes tells us the letters of the phrase to hamper are rearranged into a new word

explanation.surface: A business leader sets about obstructing reforms.
explanation.walkthrough: 'changes' rearranges TO HAMPER. The definition works because no captain of industry actually steers a ship: the phrase is figurative.
explanation.definitionFit: Calling a tycoon a captain is a figure of speech, transferring a ship's commander onto a businessman.

clue.text: Well considered to remove freedom?

definitions.meaning: describes a choice made carefully and on purpose
playfully read as DE- plus a verb meaning to set free, so undoing a release

explanation.surface: Is taking away someone's liberty a thoughtful act?
explanation.walkthrough: The second sense is a pun: the prefix DE- undoes 'liberate' (free), and the question mark flags the invented word.
explanation.definitionFit: A deliberate act is intentional and weighed up; split as de-liberate it would mean un-freeing someone.

clue.text: Caught by noisy rush in sudden shower

parts.note: C is the cricket abbreviation for caught
noisy means loud
a burst is a sudden rush, as in a burst of speed

explanation.surface: Someone gets caught out by a loud rush during an unexpected downpour.
explanation.definitionFit: A brief, heavy downpour of rain arriving without warning.

clue.text: Among others, Q-tip was unusually black

indicators.note: unusually signals that the letters of was and the black abbreviation are put into an unusual order

parts.note: B is the standard abbreviation for black, as on pencils

explanation.surface: One particular cotton bud stood out for being an odd black colour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unusually' rearranges WAS plus B (black) into the answer. Q-tip is a brand of cotton bud, given as one example among others.
explanation.definitionFit: A Q-tip is a branded cotton bud, one kind of small absorbent pad on a stick used for cleaning.

clue.text: Nothing right on a Latin viva

parts.note: nothing is zero, the letter O

explanation.surface: A student gets no credit for an oral exam in Latin.
explanation.walkthrough: A viva is a spoken university examination, from the Latin viva voce.
explanation.definitionFit: A viva voce is a spoken examination, so the exam is conducted by mouth.

clue.text: Parcel formed of British booze

parts.note: ale is a kind of booze, beer

explanation.surface: A package made up of British alcohol.
explanation.definitionFit: A bale is a large bound bundle of goods, such as hay or cotton, so a kind of parcel.

clue.text: What a tissue is said to be for!

definitions.text: What a tissue is said to be for!

parts.words: What a tissue is said to be for
parts.note: spoken, a tissue sounds like the noise atishoo, so the clue asks what that noise is for as well as what a paper handkerchief is used for

explanation.surface: A remark on the purpose of a paper handkerchief.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a tissue' said quickly is 'atishoo', the sound of the act; and a tissue is also what you reach for when it happens.
explanation.definitionFit: Atishoo is the conventional written sound of this explosive nasal reflex, and tissues catch it.

clue.text: Show about meat

parts.note: re means about, concerning
veal is calf meat

explanation.surface: A display concerning meat.
explanation.definitionFit: To show something is to disclose or uncover it.

clue.text: With a Received Pronunciation "isn't" gets slap?

parts.note: RP is the standard abbreviation for Received Pronunciation, the prestige British accent
ain't is a colloquial form of isn't

explanation.surface: Someone using a posh accent says 'ain't' and is smacked for it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'slap' is British slang for make-up, not a blow; Received Pronunciation is the 'BBC' accent of southern England.
explanation.definitionFit: Slap is theatrical slang for make-up, and war paint is a jokey term for heavy cosmetics.

clue.text: Make heavy demands on current people carrier?

parts.note: to tax someone is to strain or burden them
I is the symbol for electric current

explanation.surface: Asking a lot of the latest family car.
explanation.walkthrough: 'people carrier' suggests a family minivan; the question mark admits it means any vehicle carrying passengers.
explanation.definitionFit: A cab carries paying passengers, so it is a vehicle for transporting people.

clue.text: Reuben & Levi converted atheist

indicators.note: converted means the letters of the two names are changed into a different form

explanation.surface: Two men with Biblical names have turned to disbelief.
explanation.walkthrough: 'converted' rearranges REUBEN and LEVI, and plays on religious conversion, ironically towards no faith.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who denies God's existence lacks religious belief.

clue.text: Start to shove till this goes about a foot

indicators.note: start to means only the opening letter of the next word is taken

parts.note: to till soil is to hoe it

explanation.surface: Push something until it wraps around a foot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'till' looks like 'until' but is the verb for working soil.
explanation.definitionFit: Footwear encloses the foot, so this item goes around it.

clue.text: Depardieu's good starting to kiss, eg Keaton, in such a film

parts.note: Gerard Depardieu is French, and bon is French for good

indicators.note: starting to takes only the first letter of the following word

parts.note: Buster Keaton was a silent film comedian

explanation.surface: A French actor starts kissing a silent comedian in a racy movie.
explanation.walkthrough: A bonkbuster is a racy blockbuster (British slang 'bonk' means have sex); the whole clue paints the scene, with 'such a film' the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A sexually explicit popular blockbuster, usually a novel or its screen adaptation.

clue.text: Snow Queen dictates when hell freezes over?

parts.note: névé is granular snow on a glacier
R is the abbreviation for Regina, queen

explanation.surface: The Snow Queen declares that something will only happen once hell has frozen.
explanation.walkthrough: NÉVÉ is the mountaineers' word for compacted granular snow.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom for an event that will not ever happen, at no time at all.

clue.text: Grissino? Perhaps change jam

parts.note: bread is slang for money, and loose change is an example of money
to jam is to stick fast

explanation.surface: Asking whether an Italian snack might swap jams.
explanation.walkthrough: 'change' means coins and 'bread' is slang for money; 'jam' is a verb, not the spread.
explanation.definitionFit: Grissini are thin, crisp Italian baked rods of dough.

clue.text: Add lithe players over time

indicators.note: in a down clue the players sit over, above, the time letter

parts.note: lithe means supple
players in a team are men

explanation.surface: Bring in agile players for extra time.
explanation.definitionFit: To supplement is to add something extra to make up a whole.

clue.text: Solo invariably stops

indicators.note: stops means the answer is stopped up, held inside the word invariably

explanation.surface: A soloist always comes to a halt.
explanation.definitionFit: An operatic song for a single voice.

clue.text: Show receipts ignoring what gent holds

indicators.note: ignoring tells us to leave out the named letters

parts.note: revenue is money received, receipts
the middle of the word gent is EN

explanation.surface: Showing your receipts while overlooking what a gentleman carries.
explanation.definitionFit: A theatrical entertainment of sketches and songs.

clue.text: Part of step, a certain distance

indicators.note: Part of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A stride covers a set length.
explanation.definitionFit: A pace is a unit of length, roughly one stride.

clue.text: Tea remains unfinished before homely padre

indicators.note: unfinished means the word loses its last letter

parts.note: char is British slang for tea
homely means plain, unattractive

explanation.surface: Tea stays undrunk as a plain-living clergyman arrives.
explanation.walkthrough: 'remains' is a link verb, not leftovers; 'homely' is used in the American sense of plain-looking.
explanation.definitionFit: Padre is the informal title for a military or institutional clergyman.

clue.text: St Charlie rose getting Joe Public's support?

parts.note: St is the abbreviation for street, here expanded
Charlie is C in the NATO alphabet
rose is a colour, red

explanation.surface: A saint called Charlie stands up and wins popular backing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'St' looks like Saint but stands for Street, expanded rather than abbreviated; 'rose' is the colour, not the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: Credibility among ordinary young people, standing with the man on the street.

clue.text: Pitch to achieve objective

parts.note: pitch is tar
to achieve is to get

explanation.surface: Throwing to reach a goal.
explanation.definitionFit: An aim or goal one is trying to hit.

clue.text: Lounge area in reduced upper room

indicators.note: in places the area letter inside the shortened room
reduced means the word loses its last letter

parts.note: a loft is a room at the top of a house

explanation.surface: A lounging space set in an attic conversion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lounge' is a verb (to idle), not a room.
explanation.definitionFit: To lounge is to idle or laze about.

clue.text: Fools handle part of transmission

parts.note: cranks are eccentric people, fools
a haft is the handle of a tool or weapon

explanation.surface: Idiots grip a component of the gearbox.
explanation.walkthrough: 'transmission' is a car's drivetrain, not broadcasting.
explanation.definitionFit: The rotating shaft in an engine that turns pistons' motion into rotation for the drivetrain.

clue.text: Good to escape dig as nature intended?

indicators.note: to escape means the letter gets out, removed from the word

parts.note: a dig in the ribs is a nudge

explanation.surface: Escaping digging as a naturist would.
explanation.walkthrough: 'as nature intended' is a stock euphemism for wearing no clothes.
explanation.definitionFit: Without clothing, the way a person is born.

clue.text: Son on jump's self-satisfied

indicators.note: in a down clue, on puts the son letter on top of the next piece

parts.note: to jump someone is to mug them

explanation.surface: A boy pleased with himself for leaping.
explanation.definitionFit: Complacent, too pleased with oneself.

clue.text: Scotland holds back man who's scored the highest

indicators.note: back means the held letters are read in the opposite direction
holds says the answer is held inside the word Scotland

explanation.surface: Scotland keeps back the man with the top score.
explanation.walkthrough: 'holds' hides OTLA in Scotland, and 'back' turns it round. A male alto sings a part scored higher than any other man's.
explanation.definitionFit: The countertenor or male alto voice part is written above tenor, the highest a man sings.

clue.text: Exploit kind monsieur first

indicators.note: first puts the monsieur letter at the front

parts.note: ilk means kind or type

explanation.surface: Take advantage of a nice Frenchman before anyone else.
explanation.walkthrough: 'kind' is a noun (sort), not the adjective it looks like.
explanation.definitionFit: To milk something is to take every advantage from it.

clue.text: Study fair and make changes again

parts.note: to read a subject is to study it
fair means just

explanation.surface: Research a fair and revise it once more.
explanation.definitionFit: To readjust is to alter or adapt something a second time.

clue.text: Plain office was good enough

parts.note: the offices is an old euphemism for the lavatory, and can is slang for a toilet
did as in that did, meaning sufficed

explanation.surface: An ordinary office was adequate.
explanation.walkthrough: 'office' is a coy word for the toilet; 'Plain' means frank.
explanation.definitionFit: Plain-spoken and frank, saying things openly.
